answer: In an orchard marketplace, each AI agent bidding to write a sonnet must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, and each deposit supports only one active bidder. A tide of fake identities therefore buys no free influence: controlling 1,000 bidders requires locking $100,000. The attacker can still create names cheaply, but scaling their bidding presence ties up capital for a month and sacrifices its use elsewhere.
